notes:
Summary: Strato TicketBridge builds a conversational agent layer for enterprise support platforms; they want to offload repetitive contact center tasks (create/update tickets, automated refunds, prioritized escalations) while keeping full audit trail and PCI-safe flows. Current stack: Zendesk + in-house refund microservice (internal API).

Recent contact: 2026-03-10 call w/ AE + SE + Head of Platform (J. Morales). Demo on 2026-02-24 (Fireflies id ff_2026-02-24_8b3f2a).

Key requirements (shorthand):
- Tool-calling: must be able to call internal refund API and Zendesk create/update; idempotency and retry rules required.
- Authorization: only certain intents allowed to trigger refunds; need role-based rule enforcement and audit log per token.
- Latency: aim for <120ms P99 for token forwarding/intent detection in agent assist; background ticket summarization can be async.
- Throughput: peak spikes up to 4k concurrent agent sessions (Black Friday simulation). Autoscale predictability a must.
- Model preferences: prefer open models + cust-tuned policies; want deterministic tool-calling behavior and structured output (JSON).
- Resiliency: fallbacks to simpler flow (create stub ticket + human triage) on model outage.
- Compliance: SOC2 + PCI sign-off required for refund flows; data residency in US required for payment tokens.

Notes from call (fragments):
- "If the system can 95% auto-handle refunds, ops head will push for pilot."
- SE flagged: need request-level tracing and request IDs surfaced in logs.
- Legal: wants architecture diagram showing no card data in LLM logs — KMS + tokenization enforced.
- Current POC: small pilot with agent assist summarization running on local infra; want Redwood Dedicated sandbox to test tool-calls.
